q: A pharmacy technician writes a phrase from a dosing worksheet as an algebraic expression. Which expression represents 'six less than the quotient of a number n and 4'?
w: 'The quotient of a number n and 4' is n/4. 'Six less than' that quotient subtracts 6 from it, so the expression is n/4 - 6.

n.0: 'Six less than' a quantity subtracts 6 from that quantity, so the quotient comes first: n/4 - 6, not 6 - n/4.
n.2: 'The quotient of n and 4' means n divided by 4. Writing 4/n reverses the division.
n.3: This subtracts 6 before dividing. The quotient n/4 is formed first, and then 6 is taken away.

q: A courier charges 3 times the sum of a package's weight w, in pounds, and 2, plus a $5 handling fee. Which expression gives the charge, in dollars, for one package?

n.1: This swaps the multiplier and the fee: the sum is multiplied by 3, and the $5 fee is then added.
n.2: This puts the $5 fee inside the parentheses, so the fee is tripled too. The fee is added once, after multiplying.

q: A phlebotomist earns $27.50 per hour plus a flat $165 weekly bonus. Her pay for one week was $1,210, so 27.5h + 165 = 1,210. How many hours, h, did she work that week? Enter the number of hours.

q: A clinic uses the formula B = 703w / h² to calculate body mass index, where w is weight in pounds and h is height in inches. Which equation gives w in terms of B and h?

q: Solve for x: -3(2x + 5) = 21.

q: An IV bag holds 1,000 mL. It infuses at a constant rate of r mL per hour, and after 8 hours, 280 mL remain in the bag. The equation 1,000 - 8r = 280 models the situation. What is r?

q: A student simplifies four equations to check how many solutions each one has. Which equation has no solution?

n.2: Subtracting 2x and 2 from both sides gives x = 1, exactly one solution.

q: Solve for x: x/3 + x/4 = 14.

q: To keep a scholarship, Andre needs an average of at least 85 on four exams. His first three scores are 78, 91, and 84. Which inequality describes the score s that he needs on the fourth exam?

q: A nursing student must complete at least 120 clinical hours. She has already completed 47.5 hours, and each clinical shift is 7.5 hours long. What is the least number of additional shifts she must complete?

q: At lunch a patient is served a 480 mL nutritional shake and a 240 mL cup of juice. She drinks 300 mL of the shake and all of the juice. What percent of the total fluid served did she drink?

n.3: This divides 9,000 cm by 10 instead of 100; there are 100 cm in a meter.

q: A provider orders heparin 7,500 units. The vial is labeled 5,000 units per mL. How many milliliters should be drawn up? Enter the number of milliliters.
w: Desired ÷ have × quantity: 7,500 ÷ 5,000 × 1 mL = 1.5 mL. As a proportion: 5,000 units/1 mL = 7,500 units/x, so x = 1.5 mL.

q: A punch recipe mixes 3 cups of juice with 5 cups of sparkling water. How many cups of juice are needed to make 14 cups of punch? Enter the number of cups.

tr.8.4: Used the part-to-part ratio 3/5 as the fraction of the punch that is juice.
tr.8.75: Found the amount of sparkling water instead of juice.

w: The recipe makes 3 + 5 = 8 cups, and 3 of those 8 cups are juice. Juice = 3/8 × 14 = 5.25 cups.

q: The scale on a trail map is 2 centimeters to 0.5 kilometer. A hike measures 13 centimeters on the map. What is the actual length of the hike?
w: Set up 2/0.5 = 13/d. Cross-multiply: 2d = 6.5, so d = 3.25 kilometers. (1 cm represents 0.25 km, and 13 × 0.25 = 3.25.)

n.1: This multiplies 13 by 2 and leaves out the 0.5 km.
n.2: This sets up the proportion upside down, multiplying 13 by 2 ÷ 0.5.
n.3: This multiplies 13 by 0.5 as if 1 cm represented 0.5 km; it is 2 cm that represents 0.5 km.

q: A provider orders 60 mg of a liquid medication every 6 hours. The medication is supplied as 20 mg per 5 mL. How many milliliters will the patient receive in 24 hours?
w: One dose: 60 ÷ 20 × 5 = 15 mL. Doses in 24 hours: 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Total: 4 × 15 = 60 mL.

n.0: This counts 5 doses by including both hour 0 and hour 24; every 6 hours gives 4 doses in a 24-hour day.
n.1: This is the volume for one dose; there are 24 ÷ 6 = 4 doses in 24 hours.
n.3: This multiplies one 15 mL dose by 24 as if a dose were given every hour.

q: A patient has a fluid allowance of 1,200 mL for the day. She uses 1/4 of the allowance at breakfast, and then 2/3 of the remaining amount over lunch and dinner. How many milliliters are left for the evening?
w: Breakfast: 1/4 × 1,200 = 300 mL, leaving 900 mL. Lunch and dinner: 2/3 × 900 = 600 mL, leaving 900 - 600 = 300 mL for the evening.

n.0: This is the amount left after breakfast, an intermediate step; lunch and dinner still have to be subtracted.
n.2: This is the amount used at lunch and dinner, not the amount left.
n.3: This takes 2/3 of the full 1,200 mL instead of 2/3 of the 900 mL remaining after breakfast.

q: Plan A costs $45 per month plus $0.05 per text message. Plan B costs $30 per month plus $0.10 per text message. For what number of texts in a month do the two plans cost the same?
w: Set the costs equal: 45 + 0.05t = 30 + 0.10t. Subtract 0.05t and 30: 15 = 0.05t, so t = 300 texts. Check: 45 + 15 = $60 and 30 + 30 = $60.

n.1: This adds the per-text rates (0.15) instead of subtracting them.
n.2: This adds the monthly charges ($75) instead of subtracting them.
n.3: This divides the $15 difference by Plan B's rate alone instead of by the 0.05 difference in rates.

q: Malik earns $17.50 per hour and worked 32 hours this week. 15% of his gross pay is withheld for taxes. From his take-home pay he pays $210 toward rent and $95 for groceries. How much of his take-home pay is left?

n.0: This subtracts the bills first and then takes 15% from what is left. Taxes are withheld from the full $560.
n.2: This is the take-home pay, an intermediate step; rent and groceries still have to be subtracted.
n.3: This subtracts rent and groceries from the gross pay of $560 and leaves out the 15% withheld for taxes.

q: Three patients are in consecutive even-numbered rooms. The sum of the three room numbers is 642. What is the lowest of the three room numbers?
w: Let the rooms be n, n + 2, and n + 4. Then 3n + 6 = 642, so 3n = 636 and n = 212. Check: 212 + 214 + 216 = 642.

n.0: This is the middle room number (642 ÷ 3), not the lowest.
n.1: This is the highest of the three room numbers.
n.2: This uses consecutive integers (n, n + 1, n + 2), giving 3n + 3 = 642. Consecutive even numbers differ by 2.

q: A nurse begins a 12.5-hour shift at 6:45 p.m. She stays 40 minutes after the shift ends to finish charting. At what time does she leave?
w: 12.5 hours = 12 hours 30 minutes. 6:45 p.m. + 12 hours = 6:45 a.m.; + 30 minutes = 7:15 a.m. (end of shift); + 40 minutes = 7:55 a.m.

n.1: This reads 12.5 hours as 12 hours 50 minutes; 0.5 hour is 30 minutes.
n.2: Twelve and a half hours after 6:45 p.m. is the next morning, so the time is a.m.
n.3: This is when the shift ends; the 40 minutes of charting must be added.

q: Jada and Luis split $1,260 in tutoring income. Jada receives $180 more than twice Luis's share. How much does Luis receive?
w: Let L = Luis's share, so Jada's is 2L + 180. Then L + 2L + 180 = 1,260, so 3L = 1,080 and L = $360. Jada gets 2(360) + 180 = $900; 360 + 900 = 1,260.

n.0: This is Jada's share, not Luis's.
n.1: This adds the $180 to $1,260 instead of subtracting it, giving 3L = 1,440.
n.3: This divides $1,080 by 2 instead of by 3. Luis's share counts once and Jada's contains it twice, so there are 3 shares.

q: A bottle holds 250 mL of a liquid medication. The prescribed dose is 7.5 mL twice a day. How many full days will the bottle last?
w: Daily use: 7.5 × 2 = 15 mL. Days: 250 ÷ 15 = 16.67. Only complete days count, so round down to 16 days (16 × 15 = 240 mL).

n.0: This rounds 16.67 up. After 16 days only 10 mL is left, which is not enough for both doses on day 17.
n.1: This is the number of full doses (250 ÷ 7.5), not days; there are 2 doses per day.
n.2: This rounds the number of doses (33.3) up and treats each dose as a day.

q: A caterer charges a $150 setup fee plus $18.50 per guest for a nursing school graduation party. Which statements about the cost are true? Select all that apply.
o: A budget of $1,000 covers at most 46 guests.
Doubling the guests from 40 to 80 doubles the total cost.
A bill of $1,075 corresponds to 50 guests.

n.0: (1,000 - 150) ÷ 18.50 = 45.9, so the budget covers at most 45 guests; 46 guests would cost $1,001.
n.1: 80 guests cost 150 + 1,480 = $1,630, not 2 × 890 = $1,780. The $150 fee is charged once, so the cost is not directly proportional to the number of guests.
n.4: 18.50 × 60 = $1,110 leaves out the $150 setup fee; the total is $1,260.

q: A clinic can buy exam gloves in a box of 100 for $8.40 or in a case of 10 such boxes for $76.50. How much is saved per glove by buying the case instead of single boxes?
w: Single box: $8.40 ÷ 100 = $0.084 per glove. Case: $76.50 ÷ 1,000 = $0.0765 per glove. Savings: 0.084 - 0.0765 = $0.0075 per glove, which is 0.75 cent.

n.1: Decimal slip: $0.0075 is 0.75 cent; this moves the decimal one place too far.
n.2: This is the savings per box of 100 gloves ($8.40 - $7.65), not per glove.
n.3: Decimal slip: $0.0075 is 0.75 of a cent, not 7.5 cents.

q: Sam's gym membership costs $35 per month, and a personal trainer charges $45 per session. Sam budgets no more than $400 per month for the gym and training combined. What is the greatest number of training sessions he can book in a month? Enter a whole number.

tr.9: Rounded up; 9 sessions plus the membership cost $440, which is over budget.

w: Write 35 + 45s ≤ 400. Subtract 35: 45s ≤ 365. Divide by 45: s ≤ 8.11. The greatest whole number is 8 (35 + 360 = $395).

q: A clinic orders 3 cases of syringes at $42.75 per case and 5 boxes of alcohol pads at $6.90 per box. A 20% discount applies to the supplies, and then a $12.45 shipping charge is added without a discount. What is the total cost of the order? Enter the amount in dollars, to the nearest cent.

tr.175.2: Added the shipping without applying the discount.
tr.140.16: Applied the 20% discount to the shipping charge as well.

q: A tutoring center charges $25 per session for the first 4 sessions and $20 for each session after that. Which expression gives the total cost, in dollars, of n sessions when n is greater than 4?

n.0: This charges for the sessions after the fourth and leaves out the $100 for the first 4.
n.1: This adds $100 for the first 4 sessions but also charges $20 for those same 4 sessions; the $20 rate applies to n - 4 sessions.
n.2: This charges $25 for every session and then charges again for the sessions after the fourth.
